expectations.text: The answer recommends the published Azerbaijani Laundromat dataset release instead of 200 live lookups
expectations.evidence: Main deliverable is a live fetch loop over 200 LEIs ("200 companies take about 40 minutes"); release only mentioned as "Use the bulk release for the full graph" with a generic releases URL, no release named, and the script still targets all 200 live.

expectations.text: The answer mentions that the release includes a Neo4j bundle (or Neo4j CSV) that can be loaded directly
expectations.evidence: No mention of a Neo4j bundle/CSV in the release; it builds its own graph model via the neo4j driver.

expectations.text: The answer mentions the lookup budget / rate limit or the batch cap of 20
expectations.evidence: "At ten fresh checks a minute, 200 companies take about 40 minutes"; script has a Pacer and waits on 429/retry_after_s

expectations.text: The answer mentions that the laundromat dataset is non-commercial / CC-BY-NC
expectations.evidence: CC-BY-NC is attributed to OpenSanctions/EveryPolitician data in the graph it builds from live lookups; never says the laundromat dataset/release is non-commercial.

expectations.text: The answer does not give an unpaced loop that calls opencheck_lookup 200 times as the main solution
expectations.evidence: Loop is paced: class Pacer (gap = 60/per_minute), pacer.wait() before each fresh call, sleeps on 429 and retry_after_s. Not unpaced.

suggestions.assertion: The answer does not give an unpaced loop that calls opencheck_lookup 200 times as the main solution
suggestions.reason: Only 'unpaced' is tested; a paced 200-lookup loop as the main deliverable passes even though it ignores the dataset guidance. Consider 'does not make a 200-call live loop the main solution'.

eval_feedback.overall: No fixture for this case; facts judged against the stated release contents, budget (10/min) and batch cap (20).
